turns.text: Hi, welcome. To start: tell me about a project you built.
I built a chat app with websockets and a Postgres backend.
Can you explain how a hash table works?
A hash function maps the key to an index, and collisions use chaining.
What happens as the table fills up?
It resizes, so lookups stay constant on average. I would pick chaining for simplicity.
Your API was fast yesterday and slow today. How do you find the cause?
I would check recent deploys, then logs and metrics, then reproduce the slow request.

info.description:
Backend for AI Viva: a fair, auditable 15-minute viva. Faculty set up vivas and review results; students take the viva.

**Contract status:** during the contract phase every route marked as a stub returns its example payload with the header
`X-Contract-Stub: 1`, so `uvicorn` is a working mock backend. Send `X-Mock-Error: <code>` to any stub route to get that error.

**Conventions.** Errors always look like `{"error": {"code", "message", "details"}}` with a code from a fixed list.
Timestamps are ISO-8601 UTC ending in `Z`. Durations are integer milliseconds (`*_ms`). Faculty send
`Authorization: Bearer <faculty token>`; students send `Authorization: Bearer <session token>` (starts with `st_`).
Wrong role gives 403, missing or unknown token gives 401.

**Voice (TBD, task T4):** a WebSocket for live audio is reserved (planned `/student/sessions/{sid}/voice`) but is not
part of this contract and not implemented. The text endpoints below are the contract; voice will reuse the same
session, token, timer and turn numbering.
info.title: AI Viva API

Transcript, scores per run and the median, per-dimension reason and evidence, feedback, overrides, integrity
events and the audio reference. Evidence numbers are `turns[].idx`; to replay a piece of evidence seek the audio
to that turn's `t_start_ms`. `effective_total` is the latest override's `new_total`, else the AI median.

post.description:
No Authorization header. Creates the student's one session for this viva, or **rejoins** it: rejoining with
the same code is allowed while the session is `created`, `consented` or `in_progress`, returns `resumed: true`
and a **new token (the old one stops working, 401)**. Once the session has ended the code is dead
(409 `session_ended`). Wrong ID and wrong code both give the same 403 `invalid_credentials`; repeated failures
give 429 `rate_limited`. The access code is required (D10).

post.summary: Log in with student ID and access code

post.description:
**Idempotent on `client_seq`**: sending the same `client_seq` with the same `text` again returns the same reply
(`replayed: true`) and records nothing twice, so retry freely after a timeout. A reused `client_seq` with different
text, or one that skips ahead, is 409 `bad_client_seq` (`details.expected`). After the deadline the answer is
rejected with 409 `deadline_passed` and `details.closing_text`; the session is ended and later calls get
`session_ended`. `turn.ended: true` marks the closing turn. On 503 `provider_unavailable` retry the same request.
